text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.

- The state audit's findings spur the following questions: What happened to approximately half of the 109 million kuna set aside for creating jobs for the disabled? Who and when will be held responsible for the illegal spending of state fianances?

- Jews are fully accepted in Zagreb and the whole of Croatia, but are not pleased with the way the genocide committed against them in the days of the Independent State of Croatia (NDH) is being minimised, says in an interview the president of the Jewish Community in Zagreb and member of the Coordination of Jewish Communities in Croatia, Ognjen Kraus.
- The negative balance in food import in 1996 to fall to $380 million from $420 million in 1995.
- The indictment against the Bosnain Croat indicted for war crimes in the Hague, Tihomir Blaskic, is not strong enough, claims in an interview, his lawyer, Anto Nobilo.

- Scientologists wish to extend their work to Eastern Europe including Croatia, and have annouced such intentions by placing ads in Croatian newspapers. This sect has already been described as dangerous in the U.S., Great Britain, France and Germany and accused of undermining the very foundations of society. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
